summary.one_liner: A collection of 120+ interactive, test-driven Python coding interview challenges on algorithms and data structures, with Jupyter notebooks and Anki flashcards.
summary.what_it_does: Provides coding challenges organized into categories such as arrays and strings, linked lists, graphs and trees, sorting, recursion and dynamic programming, bit manipulation, and online judge-style problems. Each challenge has a challenge notebook with skeleton code and a unit test that is expected to fail until solved, plus a solution notebook with one or more reference solutions, Big-O analysis, and discussion. The repo also includes unit-tested reference implementations of data structures (linked list, stack, queue, BST, graph, min heap, trie, hash map) and algorithms (various sorts, tree and graph traversals, Dijkstra's, knapsack, sieve of Eratosthenes). An Anki coding flashcard deck is provided for spaced repetition. Several categories are listed as TODO or contribution slots.
use_cases: Practicing algorithm questions for coding interviews
Working through data structure implementations with unit tests
Studying Big-O analysis of common algorithms
Reviewing coding concepts with Anki flashcards
Comparing reference solutions to your own answers
how_to_run: Open a challenge notebook and run all cells (Cell->Run All); the unit test is expected to fail until you solve it
Check the matching solution notebook for reference solutions
notable: Challenge and solution notebooks read/write an associated unit test file for each challenge
Static notebooks viewable via nbviewer and dynamic notebooks runnable on Binder without installation
Includes an Anki coding deck for spaced repetition review
Each solution notebook includes Big-O time and space complexity discussion
Sister repo The System Design Primer is referenced for system design and OOD prep
caveats: Hints feature is marked as coming soon and not yet available
Some challenge categories and reference implementations are listed as TODO or contribution slots
Notebooks mostly contain Python solutions; other languages are described only as possible future extensions
